With sha-evidence we don't need actorVf — but we still need to know the head moved AFTER the park. Sha ≠ parked sha proves the head CHANGED since the park (the sha is IN the park comment — written AT park time). That's actually STRONGER evidence than the date comparison: the park comment's sha IS the parked head; any different current sha means the head moved. No dates needed!

So the rung: machine-authored && parkedHeadSha known && ≠ uHead && current-head verdict ≠ 'failure' → clear. Now I have the full picture. The owner contracts pinned by tests:

1. **Guests**: machine pushes / green heads / bot merges NEVER clear. Only a fresh HUMAN push clears. (fa#923, #681, #1249, gh-750)
2. **Machine PRs**: gh-750 self-clear — green rollup, or head-moved-clean — gated on `actorVf !== null && parkedAtVf !== null`.
3. **#633**: sha-known head change + no fresh red → clear (any author).

My inserted rung violates guests. The correct scoping for (b) that both honors pins AND fixes a real gap:

**The gh-750 gate `actorVf !== null && parkedAtVf !== null` makes the machine self-clear unreachable when the gh api probes fail (live CLI instability — evidenced in the incident window). The #633 rung is blocked by the same null-guard above it. So a machine PR with a stale park on a moved head holds forever during probe outages.**

But is that the incident? The incident's #1563 "approved, ai_pr_reviewed" — if machine-authored... And note something interesting in the gh-750 comment: "the rework armers list validation_failed as an in-flight blocker so no rework leg fires either — the park is permanent". Machine PRs have NO path when the gh-750 probes fail.

Decision: REPLACE my unscoped rung with a **probe-outage extension of gh-750's moved-head self-clear**:

New rung (replaces current staleParkHeadMovedClean call): fire when
- `isMachinePrU && uHead`
- NOT already cleared by gh-750 (i.e., machineUnparkVf false — placed after it)
- the park is PROVABLY stale: `parkedHeadVf` known AND ≠ uHead (from the park comment — no actor probe needed)
- `probeHeadVerdictVf() !== 'failure'` (fresh head not red — fails open like #633)
- AND (green rollup OR head moved per the comment evidence alone...)

Hmm — but wait, for machine PRs with WORKING probes, gh-750's headMovedCleanVf already covers head-moved-clean (probe-based). With sha-evidence we don't need actorVf — but we still need to know the head moved AFTER the park. Sha ≠ parked sha proves the head CHANGED since the park (the sha is IN the park comment — written AT park time). That's actually STRONGER evidence than the date comparison: the park comment's sha IS the parked head; any different current sha means the head moved. No dates needed!

So the rung: machine-authored && parkedHeadSha known && ≠ uHead && current-head verdict ≠ 'failure' → clear. This is #633's exact ruling extended to machine PRs — wait, #633 is ALREADY author-agnostic! #633 fires for machine PRs too when reachable. The ONLY gap: the null-guard (`actorVf === null || parkedAtVf === null`) blocks #633. And when probes work but sha is null (legacy parks), gh-750's date-based headMovedCleanVf covers machine PRs.

So the real fix: **make #633 reachable when the park sha is known, regardless of actorVf/parkedAtVf probe failures** — because #633's evidence (comment sha vs current sha + fresh verdict probe) doesn't depend on those probes at all. Move the sha-stale check BEFORE the null-guard (or exempt it):

```js
if (headChangedNoVerdictVf) {  // #633 — no probe dependency beyond the verdict probe
    ...clear...
} else if (actorVf === null || parkedAtVf === null) {
    ...hold...
}
```

It never needed actorVf/parkedAtVf. The current code evaluates it BEFORE the null-guard branch already (it's computed above, and the if-chain checks `actorVf === null || parkedAtVf === null` FIRST). Reordering so #633 is checked first: when probes work AND sha known AND differs → #633 fires (same as before). Now I understand the machineSmAgent structure. The gate at line 373: `activeIssues = provider.activeMachineRuns(cfg.workflowFile)` — if ≥ cap → idle. The gh-952 fix: filter out orphaned runs — runs whose linked issue's PR is MERGED (can never be consumed). The test expects:

1. activeIssues [1661], 1661's PR MERGED → gate releases: `out.idle` undefined, dev leg dispatches for 2001, `recorded.closed` [1661] (closeIssue called for the merged-PR issue — the Fixes #N safety net).
2. activeIssues [2001], 2001 OPEN → idle true, waitingFor ['2001'], no dispatch.
3. activeIssues [1661, 2001], 1661 MERGED, 2001 OPEN → idle true, waitingFor [2001].

So the implementation: before the gate, partition activeIssues into orphaned (linked PR merged) and live. For orphaned: log + closeIssue(issue) (safety net — matches test expectation `recorded.closed` [1661]). Then gate only on live runs.

How to check "linked PR is MERGED"? `provider.findPr(issueNumber, cfg.branchPrefix)` returns `{number, state}` — state 'MERGED' or 'OPEN'; null when no PR. The test's findPr returns `{number: 1661, state: ...}` (number hardcoded 1661, whatever). Careful: for an issue with NO PR (null) — is the run orphaned? A run whose issue has no PR at all — the dev leg is running... findPr null could mean "PR not found yet" (just created) — do NOT release (fail closed: only a MERGED state proves the run can never be consumed).

arguments.content:
## What changed

gh-952 (live fa 2026-10-17: fa #1661 owner-bypass-merged while armed, queue starved 3h): (a) slot bookkeeping now releases slots held by externally-merged PRs in both places that count them, and (b) a stale `validation_failed` park on a moved head can clear during a probe outage so validate-armed re-arms the fresh head the same tick.

## Key decisions

- `js/machineSmAgent.js`: the global concurrency gate filters out **orphaned runs** — an active run whose linked PR is `MERGED` can never be consumed (gh-952 live shape). Fail-closed probe (`unknown` placeholder and unresolvable PRs stay in the count); the reconcile loop's `activeSet` now uses the live list so the dead run no longer suppresses the Fixes #N close.
- `js/sm/mergeBot.js`: when no OPEN PR holds the merge-window arm (`ai_validating` + `pr_approved` parity — a dev-lane arm never held the window), probe merged PRs once (24h recency): a recently-merged armed holder vacates the FIFO head (gh-766 dead-head parity — a validated candidate may take the turn on existing evidence) and the end-of-run self-tick still fires when nothing validated exists (the incident shape: all 7 PRs `FIFO-queued`, acted 0). The self-tick block moved verbatim into `selfTickToSm()` (CRAP ratchet).
- `js/smAgent.js` (b): the #633/gh-750 self-clear rungs both sit behind the substantive-commit/park-time probes — during the incident window's CLI outage the null-guard fail-closed HOLD every tick, making a machine park permanent. New probe-outage exemption: a **machine-authored** PR whose park comment names a parked-head sha that differs from the current head clears when the fresh head carries no red dispatched verdict (fail-open verdict probe, #633's design). Rung is machine-scoped and sha-keyed — the fa#923/#681/#1249/gh-750 guest contracts (machine pushes never speak for a guest) are untouched, verified by the untouched pinned tests.

## How to verify

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
# 2981 passed, 0 failed (suites: run_machineSmAgent 37, run_mergeBot 40,
# run_smAgent 552 — each carries a gh-952 suite)
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph machineSmAgent
    R[activeMachineRuns] --> G{linked PR MERGED?}
    G -->|orphan| DROP[drop from slot count + release log]
    G -->|live / unknown| HOLD[counts toward cap]
  end
  subgraph mergeBot
    O[open PRs] -->|no armed holder| M[probe merged list 24h]
    M -->|armed + fresh| V[vacate FIFO head]
  end
  subgraph smAgent park ladder
    P[park probes failed] -->|machine PR + park-comment sha differs + no fresh red| C[clear label + cache drop]
    P -->|guest / sha equal / fresh red| KEEP[keep park fail-closed]
  end
```

</details>

Now I understand the machineSmAgent structure. The gate at line 373: `activeIssues = provider.activeMachineRuns(cfg.workflowFile)` — if ≥ cap → idle. The gh-952 fix: filter out orphaned runs — runs whose linked issue's PR is MERGED (can never be consumed). The test expects:

1. activeIssues [1661], 1661's PR MERGED → gate releases: `out.idle` undefined, dev leg dispatches for 2001, `recorded.closed` [1661] (closeIssue called for the merged-PR issue — the Fixes #N safety net).
2. activeIssues [2001], 2001 OPEN → idle true, waitingFor ['2001'], no dispatch.
3. activeIssues [1661, 2001], 1661 MERGED, 2001 OPEN → idle true, waitingFor [2001].

So the implementation: before the gate, partition activeIssues into orphaned (linked PR merged) and live. For orphaned: log + closeIssue(issue) (safety net — matches test expectation `recorded.closed` [1661]). Then gate only on live runs.

How to check "linked PR is MERGED"? `provider.findPr(issueNumber, cfg.branchPrefix)` returns `{number, state}` — state 'MERGED' or 'OPEN'; null when no PR. The test's findPr returns `{number: 1661, state: ...}` (number hardcoded 1661, whatever). Careful: for an issue with NO PR (null) — is the run orphaned? A run whose issue has no PR at all — the dev leg is running... findPr null could mean "PR not found yet" (just created) — do NOT release (fail closed: only a MERGED state proves the run can never be consumed).

Wait, but also `closeIssue` for the orphan — the test expects it. And what about the reconciliation loop — the issue 1661 is also in listMachineIssues output with label 'ai_developed'. {"content":"## What changed

gh-952 (live fa 2026-10-17: fa #1661 owner-bypass-merged while armed, queue starved 3h): (a) slot bookkeeping now releases slots held by externally-merged PRs in both places that count them, and (b) a stale `validation_failed` park on a moved head can clear during a probe outage so validate-armed re-arms the fresh head the same tick.

## Key decisions

- `js/machineSmAgent.js`: the global concurrency gate filters out **orphaned runs** — an active run whose linked PR is `MERGED` can never be consumed (gh-952 live shape). Fail-closed probe (`unknown` placeholder and unresolvable PRs stay in the count); the reconcile loop's `activeSet` now uses the live list so the dead run no longer suppresses the Fixes #N close.
- `js/sm/mergeBot.js`: when no OPEN PR holds the merge-window arm (`ai_validating` + `pr_approved` parity — a dev-lane arm never held the window), probe merged PRs once (24h recency): a recently-merged armed holder vacates the FIFO head (gh-766 dead-head parity — a validated candidate may take the turn on existing evidence) and the end-of-run self-tick still fires when nothing validated exists (the incident shape: all 7 PRs `FIFO-queued`, acted 0). The self-tick block moved verbatim into `selfTickToSm()` (CRAP ratchet).
- `js/smAgent.js` (b): the #633/gh-750 self-clear rungs both sit behind the substantive-commit/park-time probes — during the incident window's CLI outage the null-guard fail-closed HOLD every tick, making a machine park permanent. New probe-outage exemption: a **machine-authored** PR whose park comment names a parked-head sha that differs from the current head clears when the fresh head carries no red dispatched verdict (fail-open verdict probe, #633's design). Rung is machine-scoped and sha-keyed — the fa#923/#681/#1249/gh-750 guest contracts (machine pushes never speak for a guest) are untouched, verified by the untouched pinned tests.

## How to verify

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
# 2981 passed, 0 failed (suites: run_machineSmAgent 37, run_mergeBot 40,
# run_smAgent 552 — each carries a gh-952 suite)
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
```

{"content":"## What changed

gh-952 (live fa 2026-10-17: fa #1661 owner-bypass-merged while armed, queue starved 3h): (a) slot bookkeeping now releases slots held by externally-merged PRs in both places that count them, and (b) a stale `validation_failed` park on a moved head can clear during a probe outage so validate-armed re-arms the fresh head the same tick.

## Key decisions

- `js/machineSmAgent.js`: the global concurrency gate filters out **orphaned runs** — an active run whose linked PR is `MERGED` can never be consumed (gh-952 live shape). Fail-closed probe (`unknown` placeholder and unresolvable PRs stay in the count); the reconcile loop's `activeSet` now uses the live list so the dead run no longer suppresses the Fixes #N close.
- `js/sm/mergeBot.js`: when no OPEN PR holds the merge-window arm (`ai_validating` + `pr_approved` parity — a dev-lane arm never held the window), probe merged PRs once (24h recency): a recently-merged armed holder vacates the FIFO head (gh-766 dead-head parity — a validated candidate may take the turn on existing evidence) and the end-of-run self-tick still fires when nothing validated exists (the incident shape: all 7 PRs `FIFO-queued`, acted 0). The self-tick block moved verbatim into `selfTickToSm()` (CRAP ratchet).
- `js/smAgent.js` (b): the #633/gh-750 self-clear rungs both sit behind the substantive-commit/park-time probes — during the incident window's CLI outage the null-guard fail-closed HOLD every tick, making a machine park permanent. New probe-outage exemption: a **machine-authored** PR whose park comment names a parked-head sha that differs from the current head clears when the fresh head carries no red dispatched verdict (fail-open verdict probe, #633's design). Rung is machine-scoped and sha-keyed — the fa#923/#681/#1249/gh-750 guest contracts (machine pushes never speak for a guest) are untouched, verified by the untouched pinned tests.

## How to verify

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
# 2981 passed, 0 failed (suites: run_machineSmAgent 37, run_mergeBot 40,
# run_smAgent 552 — each carries a gh-952 suite)
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph machineSmAgent
    R[activeMachineRuns] --> G{linked PR MERGED?}
    G -->|orphan| DROP[drop from slot count + release log]
    G -->|live / unknown| HOLD[counts toward cap]
  end
  subgraph mergeBot
    O[open PRs] -->|no armed holder| M[probe merged list 24h]
    M -->|armed + fresh| V[vacate FIFO head]
  end
  subgraph smAgent park ladder
    P[park probes failed] -->|machine PR + park-comment sha differs + no fresh red| C[clear label + cache drop]
    P -->|guest / sha equal / fresh red| KEEP[keep park fail-closed]
  end
```

</details>

The rung is deliberately machine-scoped and sha-keyed — an unscoped version re-opens the pinned fa#1094 live fire (machine pushes cycling guest re-arms every tick), which the untouched fa#923/#681/#1249/gh-750 tests confirm.
